scenarios.name: Barbershop Booking System
scenarios.context: A local barbershop currently manages all appointments through walk-ins and telephone calls. The owner wants to digitalise the booking process to reduce no-shows, manage multiple barber schedules, and allow customers to book online outside of business hours.
scenarios.goal: Elicit the requirements for a digital appointment booking system for a small barbershop

ground_truth_requirements.statement: The system shall allow customers to book appointments online at any time, selecting a service, barber, and available time slot.
The system shall allow customers to cancel or reschedule existing appointments online without contacting the shop.
The system shall send automated SMS and email reminders to customers 24 hours and 1 hour before their appointment.
The system shall send an immediate booking confirmation to the customer via SMS and email upon successful appointment creation.
The system shall allow each barber to independently set and update their own availability, including working hours, breaks, and time off.
The system shall prevent double bookings by reflecting barber availability in real time across all booking interfaces.
The system shall provide the shop owner with daily and weekly booking summaries showing bookings, cancellations, no-shows, and peak times.
The system shall track customer no-show history and flag repeat offenders for manual booking review.
The system shall allow customers to create accounts to store personal details, communication preferences, and booking history.
The booking interface shall be usable on mobile devices without degradation of functionality.
The system shall be cost-effective to implement and operate within the budget constraints of a small independent business.
The system shall be easy to learn and use for both shop staff and customers with minimal training.
The system must comply with applicable data protection legislation governing storage of customer personal data.
The cancellation policy must enforce a minimum 24-hour notice period, with a one-time grace period for first-time customers.

scenarios.name: GP Clinic Patient Portal
scenarios.context: A small general practice (GP) clinic currently manages patient appointments, repeat prescription requests, and test result notifications through telephone calls and in-person visits. Reception staff are overwhelmed during peak hours. The clinic wants a patient-facing web portal to allow patients to book appointments, request repeat prescriptions, and receive test results securely online.
scenarios.goal: Elicit the requirements for a secure patient self-service portal for a GP clinic

ground_truth_requirements.statement: The system shall allow patients to book, cancel, and reschedule GP and nurse appointments online.
The system shall allow patients to submit repeat prescription requests online without a phone call.
The system shall allow patients to securely view their test results online once authorised by a clinician.
The system shall authenticate patients using a secure identity verification process before granting access to any personal health data.
The system shall allow GPs and nurses to manage their appointment schedules, including setting availability and blocking time slots.
The system shall provide an escalation pathway for patients with urgent symptoms to be flagged for same-day or emergency appointments.
The system shall integrate with the clinic's existing practice management software to synchronise appointment and patient data.
The system shall send automated reminders to patients before upcoming appointments via their preferred communication channel.
The system shall be accessible to patients with low digital literacy, including elderly users, conforming to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines.
The system shall ensure all patient data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
The system shall remain available 99.9% of the time during clinic operating hours.
The system shall be operable by reception staff with minimal additional training beyond a short onboarding session.
The system must comply with GDPR and applicable Irish data protection legislation for the storage and processing of patient health data.
The system must not allow patients to view test results before a clinician has reviewed and authorised their release.
The system must integrate with the clinic's existing practice management software without requiring full data migration.

scenarios.name: University Library Management System
scenarios.context: A university library currently manages study room bookings, book loans, renewals, and fine collection through a combination of in-person desk visits and an outdated legacy system that staff find difficult to maintain. Students frequently queue at the desk for tasks that could be self-served. The library wants a modernised web-based system that allows students to manage loans and room bookings online, while giving librarians better tools to manage inventory, enforce policies, and generate usage reports.
scenarios.goal: Elicit the requirements for a modernised university library management system covering study room booking, loan management, renewals, and fines

ground_truth_requirements.statement: The system shall allow students to search the library catalogue and check real-time availability of books and other materials.
The system shall allow students to borrow, return, and renew items online without visiting the library desk.
The system shall allow students to book study rooms online, selecting date, time slot, and room capacity.
The system shall automatically calculate and apply fines for overdue items based on configurable daily rates.
The system shall allow students to view their current loans, due dates, reservation history, and outstanding fines.
The system shall send automated email reminders to students before loan due dates and when fines are applied.
The system shall allow librarians to manage book inventory, including adding, updating, and retiring catalogue items.
The system shall provide librarians with usage reports covering loan volumes, popular items, room utilisation, and fine revenue.
The system shall allow librarians to place holds or restrictions on student accounts with outstanding fines above a configurable threshold.
The system shall be accessible via university single sign-on (SSO) so students and staff do not require separate credentials.
The system shall be usable on mobile devices without degradation of core booking and loan management functionality.
The system shall load catalogue search results within three seconds under normal network conditions.
The system shall conform to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards to support students with disabilities.
The system must integrate with the university student record system to verify enrolment status before permitting loans or room bookings.
The system must comply with GDPR for storage and processing of student borrowing and fine history data.
Students with outstanding fines above the maximum threshold must be blocked from making new loans or room bookings until fines are cleared.
The new system must migrate existing loan and student account data from the legacy system without data loss.

scenarios.name: University Student Portal Enhancement
scenarios.context: A university student portal already exists and is used daily by students to access timetables, view grades, and register for modules. However, the timetable view is static and cannot be personalised, grade notifications are not available so students must manually check for updates, and there is no mechanism for students to submit feedback on modules. The university wants to enhance the existing portal with three new feature areas: personalised timetable management, automated grade and deadline notifications, and a structured module feedback system. The existing portal infrastructure, authentication, and database must be preserved.
scenarios.goal: Elicit the requirements for three enhancements to an existing university student portal: timetable personalisation, grade notifications, and module feedback

ground_truth_requirements.statement: The system shall allow students to personalise their timetable view by colour-coding modules, hiding cancelled classes, and adding personal study blocks.
The system shall allow students to export or sync their personalised timetable to external calendar applications such as Google Calendar or Outlook.
The system shall notify students automatically when a new grade is posted for any module they are enrolled in.
The system shall send automated reminders to students before upcoming assignment deadlines and exam dates.
The system shall allow students to configure their notification preferences, including channel (email, SMS, in-app) and frequency.
The system shall allow students to submit structured feedback for each module after the teaching period ends, covering content quality, delivery, and resources.
The system shall allow module coordinators to view aggregated anonymised feedback results for their modules.
The system shall allow academic administrators to generate reports on module feedback trends across departments and semesters.
All new features shall be accessible via the existing portal interface without requiring students to install additional software or create new accounts.
The enhanced portal shall perform all new features without degrading the response time of existing portal functionality.
The module feedback system shall ensure student anonymity such that neither module coordinators nor administrators can identify individual respondents.
The notification system shall deliver grade notifications within five minutes of a grade being posted by a lecturer.
All enhancements must integrate with the existing portal authentication system and must not require changes to the current student login process.
The enhancements must not require migration or modification of the existing student records database schema.
Module feedback must only be made available to coordinators after the grade submission deadline has passed to prevent feedback from influencing grading.
All student data processed by the new features must comply with GDPR and the university data retention policy.

scenarios.name: Legacy Bank Mobile App Modernisation
scenarios.context: A traditional Irish retail bank currently operates a mobile banking app that allows customers to check balances and make basic transfers. The app is widely regarded as outdated compared to fintech competitors such as Revolut and N26. Customers are churning to fintechs that offer real-time spending notifications, budgeting tools, instant card freezing, and a modern intuitive interface. The bank wants to modernise its existing app by adding fintech-style features while maintaining full compliance with Central Bank of Ireland regulations, PSD2 open banking requirements, and GDPR. The core banking system (CBS) is a legacy mainframe that cannot be replaced and must be integrated with via existing APIs.
scenarios.goal: Elicit the requirements for the modernisation of a legacy retail bank mobile app to compete with fintech offerings while preserving regulatory compliance and core banking system integration

ground_truth_requirements.statement: The app shall send customers real-time push notifications for every account transaction, including amount, merchant name, and remaining balance.
The app shall allow customers to instantly freeze and unfreeze their debit and credit cards without contacting the bank.
The app shall provide customers with automated monthly spending breakdowns categorised by merchant type such as groceries, dining, and transport.
The app shall allow customers to set personalised monthly spending budgets per category and receive alerts when approaching or exceeding them.
The app shall support biometric authentication including fingerprint and face recognition as the primary login method.
The app shall allow customers to make instant peer-to-peer payments to other bank customers and to external accounts using account number or mobile number.
The app shall provide a unified view of all customer accounts including current, savings, and credit card balances on a single home screen.
The app shall allow customers to apply for overdraft increases, personal loans, and credit limit changes directly within the app.
The app shall provide in-app live chat and AI-assisted support for common customer queries without requiring a phone call.
The app shall process and display transaction notifications within five seconds of a transaction being authorised on the core banking system.
The app shall achieve a minimum App Store and Google Play rating of 4.2 within six months of launch, benchmarked against competitor fintech apps.
The app shall be available 99.95% of the time, excluding scheduled maintenance windows communicated at least 48 hours in advance.
All sensitive customer data transmitted between the app and backend systems shall be encrypted using TLS 1.3 or higher.
The app shall be usable by customers with visual impairments, conforming to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards.
All new features must integrate with the existing core banking system via its current API layer without requiring mainframe modifications.
The app must comply with PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication requirements for all payment initiations and sensitive account access.
All customer financial data must be stored and processed within the European Economic Area in compliance with GDPR.
Any new credit or lending features must comply with Central Bank of Ireland consumer protection and responsible lending regulations.
The modernised app must maintain backwards compatibility with the existing app version for a minimum transition period of six months.
